An issue attachment containing the HTML source
GitHub Pages
GitHub Releases
questions.explanation:
GitHub Pages hosts static websites from repository content and a publishing workflow. It is appropriate for project documentation and does not provide a general-purpose server-side application runtime.

1. A development environment is not the intended persistent static-site publishing service.
2. An attached source file is not a published documentation website.
3. GitHub Pages hosts static websites from repository content and a publishing workflow. It is appropriate for project documentation and does not provide a general-purpose server-side application runtime.
4. Releases distribute versioned assets rather than host the requested static site.

questions.question: A developer is adding a GitHub Actions workflow to a repository. Where should the YAML workflow file normally be stored?
options: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/
.devcontainer/
docs/workflows/ without any file in .github/workflows/
.github/workflows/
questions.explanation:
GitHub discovers repository workflow definitions in .github/workflows using YAML files. Placing configuration there makes the automation part of the versioned project.

1. ISSUE_TEMPLATE contains issue creation templates rather than Actions workflows.
2. Dev container configuration defines a development environment, not workflow discovery.
3. An arbitrary documentation folder is not where Actions discovers workflow definitions.
4. GitHub discovers repository workflow definitions in .github/workflows using YAML files. Placing configuration there makes the automation part of the versioned project.

questions.question: An administrator must script a large file upload to Blob Storage from a server and monitor transfer progress. Which Microsoft utility is intended for command-line storage data copying?
options: Azure Data Factory pipeline authoring interface
AzCopy
Azure Storage Explorer interactive uploads
Azure Data Box offline disk transfer
questions.explanation:
AzCopy is designed to copy data to and from supported Azure Storage services through command-line operations. It handles data transfer rather than resource-governance or deployment-template export.

1. Data Factory pipelines orchestrate data movement but are not the command-line copy utility requested.
2. AzCopy supports scripted file uploads to Blob Storage with job progress and transfer status.
3. Storage Explorer is a graphical data-management tool rather than the requested command-line utility.
4. Data Box addresses offline appliance-based bulk transfer rather than direct scripted copying from this server.

questions.question: Deployment Pipeline Scenario
questions.scenario:
You create a deployment pipeline named Pipeline1 to move items from Workspace1_DEV to a new workspace named Workspace1_TEST.

You deploy all the items from Workspace1_DEV to Workspace1_TEST.

The workspace contains:
• Four notebooks
• Three lakehouses  
• Two data pipelines
• Two Dataflow Gen1 dataflows
• Three Dataflow Gen2 dataflows
• Five semantic models that each has a scheduled refresh policy

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
statements: Data from the semantic models will be deployed to the target stage.
The Dataflow Gen1 dataflows will be deployed to the target stage.
The scheduled refresh policies will be deployed to the target stage.
questions.explanation: In deployment pipelines: Data from semantic models is NOT deployed (only metadata), Dataflow Gen1 dataflows ARE deployed, and scheduled refresh policies are NOT deployed to target stages.

questions.question: An enterprise organization deploys an IaaS workload on Azure using virtual machines and virtual networks. According to the shared responsibility model, which layer of the stack is managed entirely by Microsoft rather than the customer?
options: Operating system
Applications
Physical hosts
Configurations and settings
questions.explanation:
In an IaaS deployment, Microsoft is responsible for physical hosts, physical network, and physical datacenter infrastructure, while the customer manages operating systems and applications.

1. Incorrect. In IaaS, the customer manages the operating system.
2. Incorrect. In IaaS, the customer is fully responsible for deployed applications.
3. Correct. Physical hosts are managed by Microsoft across all cloud service models including IaaS.
4. Incorrect. Configurations and settings are managed by the customer for IaaS workloads.

questions.question: A Kafka consumer writes each batch into a sink that supports deduplication by event ID. A crash can occur between sink commit and offset commit. Which sequence supports safe recovery?
options: Commit offsets first and assume a failed sink write will be replayed automatically
Disable offset persistence and rely on the process heap
Leave periodic auto-commit enabled while sink writes continue asynchronously after polling
Commit sink writes first, then offsets, and deduplicate replayed event IDs
questions.explanation:
Committing after durable processing avoids skipping unprocessed data; a crash before the offset commit can replay data, so the sink must handle duplicates. This is not an automatic exactly-once cross-system transaction.

1. Advancing offsets before durable writes risks losing data on a subsequent crash.
2. Heap-only state is lost on restart and is not a durable recovery strategy.
3. An automatic offset commit can advance past records whose asynchronous sink writes are not yet durable.
4. Committing after durable processing avoids skipping unprocessed data; a crash before the offset commit can replay data, so the sink must handle duplicates. This is not an automatic exactly-once cross-system transaction.

questions.question: Hundreds of datasets share classifications such as domain=finance and sensitivity=internal. Administrators want grants that apply according to these classifications as assets change. Which approach is appropriate?
options: Lake Formation tag-based access control with governed tag assignment and grants
Individually duplicate every table grant forever while ignoring classification changes
Use S3 filename prefixes as permissions without policy enforcement
Allow users to self-assign any privileged classification tag
questions.explanation:
LF-TBAC uses tags and tag expressions to scale grants over classified resources. Tag-assignment permissions must be governed to prevent unauthorized access expansion.

1. LF-TBAC uses tags and tag expressions to scale grants over classified resources. Tag-assignment permissions must be governed to prevent unauthorized access expansion.
2. Manual named-resource grants do not use the requested classification-driven management.
3. Names are not an authorization policy by themselves.
4. Uncontrolled privileged tag assignment can bypass the intended governance.

questions.question: An administrator wants to identify noncompliant resources without blocking new deployments during an assessment phase. Which policy effect best fits?
options: Disabled
Audit
Deny
Modify
questions.explanation:
The audit effect records noncompliance without denying the operation. It is suitable for assessing the environment before moving to an enforcement approach.

1. Disabled turns off evaluation instead of producing the desired compliance findings.
2. The audit effect records noncompliance without denying the operation. It is suitable for assessing the environment before moving to an enforcement approach.
3. Deny blocks noncompliant creation or updates rather than merely reporting.
4. Modify changes supported properties rather than only observing compliance.

questions.question: Bug reports frequently omit reproduction steps and expected results. What can maintainers configure to guide reporters toward providing this information?
options: Issue templates or issue forms
A repository description mentioning that bugs are welcome
A milestone for all incoming reports
A label applied after the report is submitted
questions.explanation:
Issue templates and forms structure the information people provide when opening reports. This reduces missing context and makes triage more consistent.

1. Issue templates and forms structure the information people provide when opening reports. This reduces missing context and makes triage more consistent.
2. A description does not structure the information requested during issue creation.
3. Milestones group existing work rather than prompt for reproduction details.
4. A label classifies a report afterward instead of collecting missing report fields.

questions.question: An authenticated API user supplies tenantId in a request body. The backend uses that value directly to query another tenant’s records. What control is missing?
options: Trust a tenantId value submitted by the frontend after its own membership check
A check that the tenant ID is syntactically valid only
Authorize the requested tenant against trusted identity claims or server-side membership before accessing its data
Check that the JWT signature is valid but never compare its tenant membership with the requested tenant
questions.explanation:
Authentication identifies the caller, while authorization determines which tenant resources the caller may access. A user-supplied tenant identifier is not proof of membership.

1. Client-side checks can be bypassed; the server must enforce the authorization boundary.
2. A valid identifier can still belong to an unauthorized tenant.
3. Authentication identifies the caller, while authorization determines which tenant resources the caller may access. A user-supplied tenant identifier is not proof of membership.
4. Authentication alone does not authorize access to a different tenant’s data.

questions.question: A solutions architect is designing an event-driven application using Amazon SQS standard queues where worker nodes poll messages. When a consumer receives a message from the queue, what happens to that message immediately upon receipt?
options: The message is permanently deleted from the queue immediately.
The message remains in the queue and becomes temporarily invisible to other consumers.
The message is automatically moved to a Dead-Letter Queue until processing finishes.
The message is locked and hidden exclusively from all consumers, including the receiving consumer.
questions.explanation:
After receipt, the message remains in the queue and is temporarily invisible to other consumers for the visibility timeout. Standard queues still use at-least-once delivery: visibility timeout reduces concurrent processing but is not an exactly-once guarantee. Consumers should be idempotent.

1. Incorrect. Messages are not automatically deleted upon receipt unless explicit or supported SDK auto-deletion features are configured after successful processing.
2. Correct. As documented, received messages remain in the queue but are temporarily hidden from other consumers via the visibility timeout.
3. Incorrect. Messages are only moved to a Dead-Letter Queue after failing multiple processing attempts if a DLQ is explicitly configured.
4. Incorrect. The message is invisible to other consumers, but it is not hidden from the consumer that received it while that consumer processes it.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of data visualization?
options: To compress data for storage
To make data insights more accessible and understandable
To encrypt sensitive information
To backup data automatically
questions.explanation: Data visualization transforms complex data into visual formats like charts and graphs to make insights more accessible and easier to understand for decision-making.

questions.question: A solutions architect is designing a batch processing application that runs calculations on large datasets. The workload is fault-tolerant and flexible regarding when it runs, but requires significant compute power. To minimize costs, the architect decides to use Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. According to AWS documentation, what characteristic best describes why Spot Instances are suitable for this workload?
options: They guarantee uninterrupted execution for mission-critical relational databases without any risk of termination.
They maintain static pricing that never changes regardless of long-term supply and demand fluctuations.
They are fully covered by Compute Savings Plans to provide an additional layer of savings on top of Spot discounts.
They utilize spare EC2 capacity available for less than the On-Demand price and are well-suited for interruptible tasks like batch jobs.
questions.explanation:
Spot Instances enable users to request unused EC2 capacity at steep discounts, making them a cost-effective choice if applications can be interrupted and are flexible about when they run, such as for batch jobs and background processing.

1. Incorrect: Spot Instances can be interrupted or terminated when AWS needs the capacity back, making them unsuitable for applications that require uninterrupted execution.
2. Spot prices vary with long-term supply and demand; the stated never-changing price guarantee is false.
3. Incorrect: Spot Instances are not covered by Savings Plans, and your spend on Spot Instances does not apply toward your Compute Savings Plans commitments.
4. Correct: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at steep discounts and are ideal for interruptible workloads such as batch jobs.

questions.question: A solutions architect is configuring network security at the subnet level in an Amazon VPC and needs to understand how network ACLs handle response traffic compared to security groups. How do network ACL rules process return traffic for an allowed inbound request?
options: Responses are automatically allowed because network ACLs remember established sessions.
Responses are not automatically allowed because network ACLs are stateless and require explicit outbound rules.
Responses are automatically allowed if the return port matches the ephemeral range defined in the security group.
Responses are blocked unless the route table contains a corresponding NAT gateway entry.
questions.explanation:
Network ACLs are stateless, which means information about previously sent or received traffic is not saved. Therefore, responses to allowed inbound traffic are not automatically permitted and must be explicitly allowed by separate outbound rules. This contrasts with security groups, which are stateful and automatically permit return traffic regardless of outbound rules.

1. Incorrect. Network ACLs do not retain state or remember established sessions; that is a characteristic of security groups.
2. Correct. Because network ACLs are stateless, outbound rules must be explicitly configured to allow responses to leave the subnet.
3. Incorrect. Security groups are stateful, but network ACLs evaluate stateless rules independently for inbound and outbound traffic without session tracking.
4. Incorrect. Route tables manage packet routing destinations, not the stateless filtering behavior of network ACL packet evaluation.

questions.question: An application runs as a service account. A developer is allowed to attach that service account to a VM, but the application still cannot read BigQuery data. Which distinction matters?
options: Attaching a service account automatically gives it every permission held by the human deployer
The deployer’s personal dataset grant automatically transfers to the attached service account
Service Account User permission alone grants BigQuery dataset read access to the workload
Permission to use the service account and the service account’s own permissions on BigQuery are separate
questions.explanation:
A service account is both an IAM resource that can be used by authorized actors and a principal granted access to other resources. Attachment permission does not grant it data access automatically.

1. The workload does not automatically inherit all human deployer permissions.
2. Human deployer access is not automatically assigned to the runtime principal.
3. Permission to attach or act as the account is distinct from its authorization on a dataset.
4. A service account is both an IAM resource that can be used by authorized actors and a principal granted access to other resources. Attachment permission does not grant it data access automatically.

questions.question: An administrator is planning a supported resource move from RG-A to RG-B within the same subscription. Which consequence should be considered for scripts that store the full resource ID?
options: The resource ID changes because its resource-group segment changes
The resource ID always stays byte-for-byte identical
The resource automatically moves to RG-B’s geographic region
The move creates a second independent copy while leaving the first unchanged
questions.explanation:
A resource ID includes its resource group. Moving a supported resource to another group changes that path, so external references to the old ID may need updating; a group move is not a regional relocation.

1. A resource ID includes its resource group. Moving a supported resource to another group changes that path, so external references to the old ID may need updating; a group move is not a regional relocation.
2. The resource-group segment cannot remain identical after the resource moves groups.
3. Changing resource groups does not itself relocate the resource’s region.
4. A move changes organization rather than cloning the resource.

questions.question: A central network team must manage subnets and firewall policy while application teams deploy resources in separate projects using that network. Which architecture fits?
options: VPC Peering alone with every application team maintaining its own independent network policy
Create a separate VPC in every service project and share only common network naming conventions
Give application projects read-only access to the host project but omit Shared VPC attachment and subnet-use grants
Shared VPC with a host project and authorized service projects
questions.explanation:
Shared VPC separates centralized network administration in a host project from workload administration in service projects. Grant subnet use and other permissions deliberately.

1. Peering connects separate VPCs but does not provide the same shared centrally administered subnet model.
2. Independent VPCs with matching names do not provide centrally managed shared subnets.
3. Read-only project access does not establish the service-project network relationship and use permissions.
4. Shared VPC separates centralized network administration in a host project from workload administration in service projects. Grant subnet use and other permissions deliberately.

questions.question: A solutions architect is designing a web application that requires advanced routing, path-based request forwarding, and TLS termination at Layer 7. Which load balancer type should the architect select to meet these requirements?
options: Classic Load Balancer
Application Load Balancer
Network Load Balancer
Gateway Load Balancer
questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer operates at layer 7 and supports advanced routing features, such as path-based and host-based routing, as well as TLS termination. A Network Load Balancer operates at layer 4, and a Gateway Load Balancer is used for deploying third-party virtual appliances.

1. Classic Load Balancer does not provide the requested path-based routing rules. Application Load Balancer is the fit for this Layer 7 routing requirement.
2. Correct: Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and is designed for HTTP/HTTPS traffic routing, path-based routing, and TLS termination.
3. Incorrect: Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and is designed for high-throughput, ultra-low latency TCP/UDP traffic routing rather than Layer 7 path inspection.
4. Incorrect: Gateway Load Balancer is designed to deploy, scale, and manage virtual third-party appliances (such as firewalls and deep packet inspection systems) at Layer 3/4.

questions.question: A financial services company is designing a disaster recovery strategy for a critical application. The company requires the recovery strategy to maintain a scaled-down, fully functional copy of the production environment running continuously in a secondary AWS Region so that traffic can be routed to it immediately at reduced capacity during a disaster event. Which disaster recovery strategy matches this description?
options: Backup and restore
Pilot light
Warm standby
Multi-site active/active
questions.explanation:
The warm standby disaster recovery approach involves maintaining a scaled-down, but fully functional, copy of your production environment in another Region. Unlike the pilot light approach where application servers are switched off and require provisioning or turning on, a warm standby environment is always on and can handle traffic immediately at reduced capacity levels before scaling up to full production load.

1. Backup and restore involves recreating the infrastructure and restoring data from backups after a disaster occurs, rather than maintaining a running copy of the environment.
2. Pilot light keeps core data stores running and replicates data, but application servers are switched off and must be deployed or turned on during a disaster.
3. Warm standby maintains a scaled-down, fully functional copy of the environment running continuously in a secondary Region, allowing it to handle traffic immediately at reduced capacity.
4. Multi-site active/active serves traffic simultaneously from multiple Regions, rather than using a secondary Region solely for standby disaster recovery.

questions.question: Development and production Glue jobs drift because engineers change scripts and job settings manually. Which two controls best support repeatable releases? Choose TWO.
options: Version the transformation code and deploy a specific reviewed artifact
Manage job definitions and dependencies through versioned infrastructure as code
Have every environment download an unpinned latest script at runtime
Rely only on unit tests while leaving production job settings as manual untracked changes
Overwrite the same script object on every release without retaining a versioned artifact reference
questions.explanation:
A reviewed versioned artifact identifies exactly which transformation logic is released and enables rollback. Versioned infrastructure complements it by defining repeatable configuration.

1. A reviewed versioned artifact identifies exactly which transformation logic is released and enables rollback. Versioned infrastructure complements it by defining repeatable configuration.
2. Infrastructure as code makes job settings and dependencies reviewable and repeatable across environments.
3. An unpinned runtime artifact can change without a controlled release.
4. Tests help correctness but do not make untracked environment configuration reproducible.
5. An overwritten mutable artifact does not reliably identify the reviewed code or support reproducible rollback.

questions.question: An engineering team is creating a new S3 Lifecycle policy for an S3 bucket containing millions of small files, many of which are under 128 KB in size. The team wants to optimize storage costs by transitioning objects to an archive tier. According to AWS documentation regarding default transition behavior, what happens to objects smaller than 128 KB?
options: They transition successfully but incur double early deletion fees upon arrival.
They transition automatically at a discounted request rate designed for small files.
They are automatically grouped into archive bundles before transitioning to S3 Glacier.
A new configuration leaves them in the current class by default; explicit overrides can permit eligible transitions.
questions.explanation:
For new S3 Lifecycle configurations, the default is to exclude objects smaller than 128 KB from transitions. An explicit object-size filter can override this behavior. The API also provides a minimum-object-size transition behavior header. Older configurations can retain their earlier behavior until modified.

1. Incorrect. Early deletion fees apply when deleting objects before their minimum storage duration, not upon arrival during transition.
2. Incorrect. There is no discounted request rate that automatically applies to small objects without explicit filtering.
3. Incorrect. S3 Lifecycle does not automatically bundle small files into archive packages; overhead charges apply per object.
4. The new-configuration default prevents small-object transitions. A size filter is an override mechanism, not the only configuration mechanism.

questions.question: Gemini Cloud Assist flags a VM as a cleanup candidate using an asset inventory snapshot and low recent utilization. The VM also runs a month-end batch not present in that metric window. What should the engineer do before deletion?
options: Refresh only the inventory timestamp and ignore utilization outside the short window
Delete after checking only that the VM has no incoming HTTP requests
Check current dependencies and a representative workload window, then follow the approved change process
Treat low utilization during the recent window as proof that month-end demand cannot exist
questions.explanation:
Recent low use and an inventory snapshot are insufficient to establish that a resource is no longer needed; include periodic workloads and current dependencies.

1. Fresh inventory does not by itself establish that periodic workload demand is absent.
2. A batch workload can be needed without serving HTTP traffic.
3. Recent low use and an inventory snapshot are insufficient to establish that a resource is no longer needed; include periodic workloads and current dependencies.
4. The observation window omits the known periodic workload.

questions.question: An IT team is evaluating the consumption-based model of cloud computing for budgeting purposes. According to Azure documentation regarding cloud financial management, how is spending on cloud services classified compared to traditional IT infrastructure?
options: Cloud services are classified as capital expenditure (CapEx) because they involve long-term vendor contracts.
Cloud services are classified as operational expenditure (OpEx) because you pay for them as you consume them over time.
Cloud services are classified as both CapEx and OpEx depending on the specific virtual machine size selected.
Cloud services are classified as non-depreciating assets that bypass traditional budgeting categories entirely.
questions.explanation:
In cloud computing, because you pay for services as you consume them rather than making a large upfront investment in physical hardware, spending is classified as an operational expenditure (OpEx). CapEx refers to traditional upfront spending on physical infrastructure.

1. Incorrect because CapEx refers to upfront spending on physical infrastructure like servers and datacenter space.
2. Correct because ongoing payments for consumed cloud services are classified as operational expenditure (OpEx).
3. Incorrect because the payment model determines the expense category, not the virtual machine size.
4. Incorrect because cloud expenses fit squarely into standard operational expenditure accounting models.

questions.question: A workspace contains a table named AppEvents with columns TimeGenerated and Severity. An administrator wants events from the last hour and counts grouped into five-minute time buckets. Select the correct KQL expression for each step.
questions.explanation:
The where operator filters input rows using the timestamp condition. summarize count() aggregates rows, and bin rounds timestamps into the requested five-minute groups.

1. where applies the timestamp condition; project only selects columns, while take 60 limits the number of rows without imposing a one-hour time window.
2. summarize count() by bin creates five-minute counts; sort only orders rows, and project Severity only selects a column without aggregation.
dropdownQuestions: Filter to rows from the last hour.
Group and count the remaining rows in five-minute buckets.

questions.question: A build creates new temporary files that should never be added to version control. Which repository file can record patterns for these untracked files?
options: .gitattributes
CODEOWNERS
.gitmodules
.gitignore
questions.explanation:
A .gitignore file records patterns for untracked files Git should ignore. It is useful for generated artifacts, but does not automatically untrack files that were already committed.

1. Attributes configure handling such as diff or line endings rather than ignoring untracked files.
2. Code ownership configures reviewer responsibility instead of ignore patterns.
3. Gitmodules records submodule configuration, not generated-file exclusions.
4. A .gitignore file records patterns for untracked files Git should ignore. It is useful for generated artifacts, but does not automatically untrack files that were already committed.

questions.question: A service needs a centrally managed group of VM instances whose instance count can grow and shrink with workload demand. Which Azure compute resource should the administrator evaluate?
options: A load balancer with no mechanism to add or remove backend VMs
A Virtual Machine Scale Set
An availability set with a fixed manually maintained VM count
A larger single VM that is resized manually
questions.explanation:
Virtual Machine Scale Sets manage groups of VM instances and support scaling their instance count. Availability placement and autoscale policy must still be configured to meet the workload’s requirements.

1. A load balancer distributes traffic but does not itself create additional compute instances.
2. Virtual Machine Scale Sets manage groups of VM instances and support scaling their instance count. Availability placement and autoscale policy must still be configured to meet the workload’s requirements.
3. An availability set does not itself manage elastic instance count.
4. Manual vertical resizing is not a centrally managed elastic group of VM instances.

questions.question: A query to a DynamoDB global secondary index briefly misses an item that was just written to the base table. The team proposes ConsistentRead=true on the GSI query. What is the correct assessment?
options: The flag makes the GSI synchronously replicate every write
A larger page Limit enables strong consistency on the GSI
Projecting all attributes into the GSI makes it strongly consistent
GSI reads are eventually consistent; use an appropriate base-table access pattern when strong consistency is required
questions.explanation:
DynamoDB global secondary indexes do not support strongly consistent reads. A base table or supported local secondary index can supply strong reads for a suitable key access pattern.

1. The request option cannot change the GSI replication and read-consistency model.
2. Page size affects result pagination, not supported consistency.
3. Projection changes stored attributes rather than consistency support.
4. DynamoDB global secondary indexes do not support strongly consistent reads. A base table or supported local secondary index can supply strong reads for a suitable key access pattern.

questions.question: An API receives a JWT that claims to identify an administrator. Which validation is essential before trusting its claims?
options: Check only that the token contains three dot-separated parts
Validate its signature with the issuer’s trusted keys and check the expected issuer, audience or client context, token use, and expiry
Base64-decode the payload and trust any admin claim
Accept any correctly signed JWT from any issuer
questions.explanation:
Decoding a JWT only reads its contents. Authentication requires cryptographic verification and the relevant claim checks for the token type and application, not merely trusting a role string.

1. Token formatting does not prove signature validity or current authorization.
2. Decoding a JWT only reads its contents. Authentication requires cryptographic verification and the relevant claim checks for the token type and application, not merely trusting a role string.
3. Unverified claims can be attacker-controlled.
4. A valid signature from an unrelated issuer does not establish the intended trust relationship.

questions.question: A company wants private connectivity from its VPC to a supported service in another AWS account without exposing that service traffic to the public internet. Which AWS service is designed for private service connectivity?
options: AWS PrivateLink
Amazon CloudFront
Amazon Route 53
AWS Global Accelerator
questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity to supported services using the AWS network. It can connect services across different accounts and VPCs without exposing that service traffic to the public internet. DNS, CDN and global traffic acceleration are different capabilities.

1. PrivateLink connects supported services privately across accounts and VPCs on the AWS network.
2. CloudFront is a content delivery network; it is not the requested private service endpoint mechanism.
3. Route 53 provides DNS services rather than private service connectivity by itself.
4. Global Accelerator optimizes application traffic through AWS networking but is not the private endpoint service described.

questions.question: A writer has permission to contribute and wants to add a small text document through GitHub’s web interface, while retaining normal review. Which approach fits?
options: Paste its contents only into an issue comment
Add the file on a new branch and open a pull request
Add the document only as a wiki page
Commit directly to the default branch and skip a pull request
questions.explanation:
GitHub’s file interface can commit a new file to a branch. Creating a pull request from that branch preserves the usual review process for the documentation change.

1. Issue comments do not add a versioned document to the repository file tree.
2. GitHub’s file interface can commit a new file to a branch. Creating a pull request from that branch preserves the usual review process for the documentation change.
3. A wiki page is separate documentation rather than the requested reviewed repository file addition.
4. Directly bypassing the pull request omits the desired review step.

questions.question: A researcher needs both a project’s current files and its Git history on a laptop. Which operation is most appropriate?
options: Copy the rendered README into a local document
Create a template-based repository and download its files
Clone the repository
Download the repository as a ZIP archive
questions.explanation:
Cloning creates a local Git repository with project files and history. This supports local version-control work rather than just obtaining a display or a single file.

1. A copied README omits both the full file tree and Git history.
2. A template supplies a new starting point rather than the original history.
3. Cloning creates a local Git repository with project files and history. This supports local version-control work rather than just obtaining a display or a single file.
4. A ZIP contains the selected files but not the Git repository history.

questions.question: Two commits change a timeout and correct a spelling mistake. Which message best supports future investigation of the timeout change?
options: Final version for now
Increase API timeout to accommodate the documented upstream latency
Update
Stuff
questions.explanation:
A meaningful commit message explains the change and useful intent. It helps reviewers and future maintainers understand the history without guessing from vague labels.

1. Final version for now describes timing rather than the actual change.
2. A meaningful commit message explains the change and useful intent. It helps reviewers and future maintainers understand the history without guessing from vague labels.
3. Update does not identify which behavior changed or why.
4. Stuff offers no useful context about the timeout change.

questions.question: A subnet has an effective route 10.50.0.0/16 to a VNet peer and a valid user-defined route 10.50.8.0/24 to an NVA. No special routing exception applies. Which route is selected for 10.50.8.25?
options: The /16 route because system routes always win
Both routes simultaneously for each packet
Neither route because their address ranges overlap
The /24 route to the NVA
questions.explanation:
Route selection first favors the longest matching prefix. The /24 is more specific than the /16 for this destination, so it is selected under the stated conditions.

1. A less-specific route does not win simply because it is a system route.
2. Azure does not automatically duplicate each packet across these differently specific routes.
3. Overlapping route prefixes are normal; longest-prefix selection resolves this case.
4. Route selection first favors the longest matching prefix. The /24 is more specific than the /16 for this destination, so it is selected under the stated conditions.

questions.question: A batch contains a small number of malformed records. Policy permits valid records to continue, but every rejected record must be recoverable. Which design fits?
options: Drop malformed rows without counts or source references
Fail all future batches permanently after the first invalid row
Replace malformed payloads with an empty successful record
Write valid results and a separately tracked quarantine dataset with source identifiers and failure reasons
questions.explanation:
A quarantine path preserves rejected data and reasons while allowing the permitted valid path to continue. Counts and lineage enable reconciliation and remediation.

1. Silent drops prevent recovery and accountability.
2. Permanent failure of unrelated future batches is not required by the policy.
3. Empty replacement records conceal errors and can corrupt output.
4. A quarantine path preserves rejected data and reasons while allowing the permitted valid path to continue. Counts and lineage enable reconciliation and remediation.

questions.question: A data pipeline uses AWS Glue crawlers and Glue cleanup jobs. Cleanup jobs must run in a dependency chain after the crawler completes. Which Glue feature coordinates this pipeline?
options: Amazon SQS dead-letter queues
Amazon CloudFront origin request policies
AWS Glue workflows with conditional triggers
Amazon EC2 auto scaling group lifecycle hooks
questions.explanation:
AWS Glue workflows organize dependent jobs and crawlers. Conditional triggers can start downstream tasks in response to the completion states of upstream tasks.

1. SQS dead-letter queues handle message delivery failures, not multi-step job workflow orchestration.
2. CloudFront origin request policies control headers and query strings sent to origins, unrelated to job orchestration.
3. AWS Glue workflows organize dependent jobs and crawlers. Conditional triggers can start downstream tasks in response to the completion states of upstream tasks.
4. EC2 auto scaling lifecycle hooks manage instance state transitions during scaling events, not data integration workflows.

questions.question: A cloud architect is establishing a new Azure account for an organization that operates separate business units. The team needs to create distinct financial billing reports and apply different access control policies for development versus production workloads. According to Azure architecture, how should the architect set up the subscriptions?
options: Deploy all workloads into a single subscription and rely entirely on resource group naming conventions for billing separation.
Create separate subscriptions for development and production to establish distinct billing boundaries and isolated access control policies.
Create nested resource groups within a single subscription to separate invoices and enforce independent billing models.
Provision a separate Azure account for each workload type, as subscriptions cannot support multiple billing models.
questions.explanation:
Subscriptions provide billing and access-control boundaries. Separate development and production subscriptions support distinct cost reporting and access policies. The final invoice structure also depends on the billing agreement.

1. Incorrect. Resource-group naming alone does not create separate subscription billing and access-control boundaries.
2. Correct. Separate subscriptions support distinct cost reporting and subscription-level access policies for the environments.
3. Incorrect. Resource groups do not generate separate invoices or isolate billing models.
4. Incorrect. An account can have multiple subscriptions, eliminating the need to create separate accounts.

questions.question: A Glue job loads a very large relational table but needs only records modified yesterday. Database network transfer dominates runtime. Which change most directly reduces transferred data?
options: Increase Spark shuffle partitions after the JDBC read
Compress the final Parquet files without changing the source query
Push the supported date predicate into the JDBC source query
Read the full table and filter only after converting to a Spark DataFrame
questions.explanation:
Filtering at the JDBC source reduces rows returned across the network when the source query supports the predicate. Verify source indexing and the actual query plan.

1. Shuffle tuning applies after ingestion and does not remove unwanted source rows.
2. Output compression reduces target storage but not source-to-job transfer.
3. Filtering at the JDBC source reduces rows returned across the network when the source query supports the predicate. Verify source indexing and the actual query plan.
4. A downstream filter after a full read has already incurred source transfer.

questions.question: A data analytics team needs to run interactive SQL queries against massive volumes of historical log data stored in Amazon S3 buckets directly in S3 using standard SQL without setting up a data warehouse. Which AWS service is the most appropriate choice?
options: Amazon Redshift
Amazon EMR
AWS Glue
Amazon Athena
questions.explanation:
Amazon Athena is a serverless interactive query service that makes it easy to analyze data in Amazon S3 using standard SQL without managing any servers or running complex ETL jobs.

1. Redshift supplies data warehousing and can query S3 through Spectrum, but Athena is the direct serverless SQL query service requested without setting up a warehouse.
2. EMR runs big-data frameworks such as Spark and Hive, including serverless options; Athena is the purpose-built interactive SQL service in this scenario.
3. AWS Glue is a fully managed extract, transform, and load (ETL) service used for data preparation and cataloging, rather than an interactive user-facing SQL query engine.
4. Amazon Athena is correct because it provides a serverless SQL query capability directly over Amazon S3 data.

questions.question: An existing pipeline should not deploy when unit tests fail. The test command currently returns a nonzero exit code, but a shell suffix suppresses it and the build succeeds. What should the developer change?
options: Move the same suppressed command into post_build without changing failure handling
Upload test reports but retain a successful build status after test failure
Preserve the test command’s failure status so the build action fails and blocks the dependent deployment
Keep suppressing the exit status and only print a failure message
questions.explanation:
A pipeline quality gate must propagate test failure into the action result. Silencing the exit status can turn a failing test suite into an apparently successful build.

1. Moving phases does not restore the discarded error status.
2. A report can show failed tests without enforcing a failed build gate if command failure is suppressed.
3. A pipeline quality gate must propagate test failure into the action result. Silencing the exit status can turn a failing test suite into an apparently successful build.
4. Log text alone does not enforce a failed pipeline action.

questions.question: A developer wants to retrieve updates from the tracked remote branch and integrate them into the current local branch. Which command is designed for this combined operation?
options: git add
git pull
git status
git branch without arguments
questions.explanation:
git pull fetches remote changes and integrates them according to the selected merge or rebase behavior. Integration may require resolving conflicts if local and remote changes overlap.

1. Add selects local changes for a future commit rather than integrating remote commits.
2. git pull fetches remote changes and integrates them according to the selected merge or rebase behavior. Integration may require resolving conflicts if local and remote changes overlap.
3. Status reports file states and does not retrieve or integrate commits.
4. Listing local branches does not update their contents.

questions.question: An App Service workload needs more worker instances of its existing SKU rather than a more powerful SKU per worker. Which operation matches this requirement?
options: Create a deployment slot without changing plan instance count
Scale out the App Service plan
Scale up to a larger pricing tier without changing instance count
Increase an application worker-process setting only
questions.explanation:
Scaling out changes the number of worker instances. Scaling up changes the pricing tier or worker capacity, while slots generally share the plan’s resources rather than automatically add workers.

1. Slots share the plan and are not an automatic increase in worker count.
2. Scaling out changes the number of worker instances. Scaling up changes the pricing tier or worker capacity, while slots generally share the plan’s resources rather than automatically add workers.
3. Scaling up changes SKU capability rather than the number of worker instances requested.
4. Application process settings do not necessarily increase the plan’s underlying worker instance count.

questions.question: A company requires strict enforcement of security policies across multiple AWS accounts in an organization. An administrator needs to restrict permissions for IAM users and ordinary IAM roles (not service-linked roles) within member accounts, ensuring that a specific unauthorized action is never allowed regardless of individual identity-based policies. Which policy type should the architect utilize?
options: An access control list (ACL) applied to an IAM user
An AWS Organizations service control policy (SCP) containing an explicit deny
An Amazon S3 object lock policy with read-only access
A default VPC endpoint policy with full access
questions.explanation:
An explicit deny in any policy (such as service control policies or identity-based policies) overrides an allow in other policies. AWS Organizations service control policies (SCPs) define maximum permissions for IAM users and roles within member accounts, and an explicit deny overrides any allow. SCPs do not grant permissions and do not restrict service-linked roles.

1. Incorrect. IAM users do not use ACLs to enforce explicit denies of AWS actions.
2. Correct. SCPs apply to member accounts, and an explicit deny within an SCP or other applicable policies overrides all allows.
3. Incorrect. Object lock governs object immutability, not general IAM action permissions across accounts.
4. Incorrect. A default VPC endpoint policy allows full access and does not restrict IAM actions across accounts.

questions.question: An operations team is evaluating Azure storage account features. They want to ensure that all data written to their storage account is protected and safeguarded. How does Azure Storage handle encryption at rest by default?
options: It requires the customer to manually encrypt each individual file via client-side keys before upload.
It automatically encrypts all data before persisting it to the storage account and decrypts it transparently upon retrieval.
It only encrypts data if the storage account is explicitly configured with a public access endpoint.
It does not support encryption at rest unless third-party virtual appliances are attached.
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage automatically encrypts all data before persisting it to the storage account and decrypts it before retrieval, making the process transparent to users.

1. Manual client-side encryption is an optional feature, not the default mechanism for standard storage account encryption at rest.
2. Automatic encryption before persistence and transparent decryption upon retrieval is correct and directly supported by the evidence.
3. Public endpoints have no direct bearing on whether data is encrypted at rest by the platform.
4. Third-party appliances are unnecessary because Azure Storage provides built-in automatic encryption at rest.

questions.question: A team wants daily VM backups retained for a short period and selected weekly recovery points retained longer. Which configuration should define these requirements?
options: Only the vault’s redundancy setting
Only an alert action group
The VM’s automatic shutdown schedule
A supported VM backup policy with the required schedule and retention settings
questions.explanation:
Backup policies define when backups run and how long recovery points are retained, subject to supported policy capabilities. Vault redundancy and notification settings address different aspects of protection.

1. Redundancy defines storage resilience, not the requested daily and weekly retention schedule.
2. Action groups configure notifications or actions rather than recovery-point retention.
3. VM shutdown timing does not define Azure Backup schedules and retention.
4. Backup policies define when backups run and how long recovery points are retained, subject to supported policy capabilities. Vault redundancy and notification settings address different aspects of protection.

questions.question: GKE Pods fail with ImagePullBackOff for a private Artifact Registry image in another project. The image reference is valid. What should be checked?
options: Grant only write access to the repository to a human deployer while the pull identity lacks read access
Assume a Kubernetes service account name automatically grants cross-project registry access
The identity used for image pulls has appropriate Artifact Registry read access and can reach the registry
Only the application’s HTTP readiness path
questions.explanation:
Private image pulls require registry authorization for the applicable pull identity plus network reachability. Cross-project access must be explicitly permitted.

1. The runtime image-pull principal needs appropriate repository access; a different human principal’s grant does not fix it.
2. A name alone does not establish IAM authorization to another project’s repository.
3. Private image pulls require registry authorization for the applicable pull identity plus network reachability. Cross-project access must be explicitly permitted.
4. Readiness probes run after the container is obtained and started.

questions.question: A learner wants to see updates from a particular developer in their GitHub activity feed without requesting access to private repositories. What should they do?
options: Request membership in an organization they belong to
Follow the developer
Watch every repository the developer owns
Star the developer’s profile README repository
questions.explanation:
Following users helps surface their public activity in the GitHub feed. It does not grant permission to private repositories or replace access-control requirements.

1. Organization membership is unnecessary to follow someone’s public updates.
2. Following users helps surface their public activity in the GitHub feed. It does not grant permission to private repositories or replace access-control requirements.
3. Watching repositories subscribes to their activity rather than following the person’s public feed.
4. Starring one repository does not follow all public activity from its owner.

questions.question: An automation needs access to a small set of repositories. Which token-management practice best limits the impact if its credential is exposed?
options: Use the organization owner’s credentials for every automation task
Store the token in the repository and rely only on private visibility
Use a suitably scoped token with only necessary repository access and permissions
Use an unrestricted long-lived token because the script currently touches few repositories
questions.explanation:
Tokens should be restricted to the resources and permissions needed by the task, with an appropriate lifecycle. Minimizing access reduces potential damage from credential exposure.

1. Owner credentials expand authority beyond the task’s narrow requirements.
2. Private visibility does not replace proper secret storage and scoped access.
3. Tokens should be restricted to the resources and permissions needed by the task, with an appropriate lifecycle. Minimizing access reduces potential damage from credential exposure.
4. The script’s present behavior does not constrain what an unrestricted stolen token could do.

questions.question: A solutions architect is evaluating traffic management options for a multi-region active/passive disaster recovery setup. The architect wants to implement a manually initiated failover mechanism using data plane APIs to toggle Route 53 health checks as on/off switches, ensuring high resiliency without relying on control plane routing weight changes. Which AWS service feature should the architect choose?
options: AWS CloudTrail multi-region event logging
AWS IAM cross-account role switching
Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC)
Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication Time Control (RTC)
questions.explanation:
Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) allows you to create Route 53 health checks that act as on/off switches controlled via high-availability data plane APIs (using the AWS CLI or SDK), enabling reliable manual failover without relying on less resilient control plane modifications.

1. AWS CloudTrail captures auditing and logging events, not DNS traffic failover routing controls.
2. IAM role switching is used for granting cross-account permissions and identity authorization, not for managing regional DNS failover.
3. Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) provides high-availability data plane routing controls to manage Route 53 health checks as switches for failover.
4. S3 Replication Time Control is used for monitoring S3 object replication latency, not for managing DNS routing failover switches.

questions.question: A company wants to assign Copilot access centrally and govern its use for employees. Why would it evaluate Business or Enterprise rather than only individual subscriptions?
options: Organization-oriented plans include centralized administration and policy controls
Organization plans mean all generated code is automatically approved
Individual subscriptions already provide identical centralized employee policy administration
Organization plans replace the need to assign user access
questions.explanation:
Copilot organization plans address centralized management such as licensing and policies. These administration capabilities do not remove developers’ responsibility to review generated code.

1. Copilot organization plans address centralized management such as licensing and policies. These administration capabilities do not remove developers’ responsibility to review generated code.
2. Administrative plans do not certify the correctness of generated code.
3. The central management requirements are why organization-oriented plans matter.
4. Organizations still manage who has access and which policies apply.

questions.question: An issue includes a multi-line Python reproduction that loses indentation when pasted as ordinary prose. What formatting should the reporter use?
options: A fenced code block, optionally marked python
Inline backticks around the entire multi-line sample
A block quote for every code line
An ordered list containing the code tokens
questions.explanation:
A fenced code block preserves the structure of multi-line code. Adding a language identifier enables syntax highlighting, making the reproduction easier to read.

1. A fenced code block preserves the structure of multi-line code. Adding a language identifier enables syntax highlighting, making the reproduction easier to read.
2. Inline code formatting is intended for short inline fragments, not a structured multi-line sample.
3. Block quotes indicate quoted prose and are not the preferred code-preserving block.
4. Numbered prose lists do not preserve the source-code structure reliably.

questions.question: An IT administrator is evaluating storage redundancy options to protect against server rack and drive failures within a single datacenter while minimizing expenses. Which primary-region redundancy option provides the lowest-cost resilience?
options: Locally redundant storage (LRS)
Zone-redundant storage (ZRS)
Geo-redundant storage (GRS)
Geo-zone-redundant storage (GZRS)
questions.explanation:
Locally redundant storage (LRS) replicates data three times within a single datacenter in the primary region and is the lowest-cost storage redundancy option in Azure.

1. Correct. LRS is the lowest-cost redundancy option and replicates data three times within a single datacenter.
2. Incorrect. ZRS replicates data across three availability zones in the primary region, which incurs a higher cost than LRS.
3. Incorrect. GRS replicates data to a secondary region, which significantly increases costs compared to primary-region-only LRS.
4. Incorrect. GZRS combines zone-redundant storage with geo-replication, representing one of the highest-cost options.
questions.topic: Storage account categories, access tiers and regional redundancy

questions.question: An API’s total latency is high, but ordinary logs do not show which downstream call consumes the time. What instrumentation best supports this diagnosis?
options: Propagate trace context and record downstream spans or subsegments in distributed tracing
Record only one aggregate request counter per minute
Log only the final HTTP status without timestamps
Increase the API timeout before collecting any latency evidence
questions.explanation:
Distributed traces connect work performed for one request and expose timing across service boundaries. Downstream timing helps distinguish application work from dependency latency.

1. Distributed traces connect work performed for one request and expose timing across service boundaries. Downstream timing helps distinguish application work from dependency latency.
2. A count lacks per-dependency timing for the slow request.
3. Status alone does not identify where request time was spent.
4. A longer timeout does not diagnose the bottleneck.

questions.question: A solutions architect is designing a multi-tier VPC architecture and reviewing subnet associations for network ACLs. If a new subnet is created within the VPC without explicitly assigning a custom network ACL, how is its network ACL association handled?
options: The subnet is automatically assigned a custom network ACL with all inbound traffic blocked by default.
The VPC creation wizard prompts for an explicit network ACL association, failing which creation is denied.
The subnet remains unassociated until a security group is attached to it.
The subnet is automatically associated with the default network ACL of the VPC.
questions.explanation:
Every subnet in a VPC must be associated with a network ACL. If a subnet is not explicitly associated with a custom network ACL, it is automatically assigned to the default network ACL for the VPC.

1. Incorrect. The default network ACL allows all inbound and outbound traffic by default, unlike custom ACLs which might have different initial configurations.
2. Incorrect. AWS automatically handles association with the default network ACL if no custom association is provided.
3. Incorrect. Subnets cannot remain unassociated with a network ACL; they are automatically assigned to the default network ACL if no custom ACL is specified.
4. Correct. Unspecified subnets automatically fall back to the default network ACL.

questions.question: An online retail organization wants to expand its application presence to multiple regions around the world to provide lower latency and a better experience for global customers. Based on AWS whitepapers, how can this be achieved?
options: Ship physical storage appliances across international borders manually.
Rely entirely on a single localized availability zone for all international traffic.
Deploy the application in multiple regions around the world with just a few clicks.
Construct custom regional data centers with long procurement cycles.
questions.explanation:
Applications can be easily deployed in multiple regions around the world with just a few clicks at minimal cost.

1. Incorrect. Manual shipping of physical storage appliances is not the cloud-native method for global deployment described.
2. Incorrect. Relying on a single zone would cause high latency for international users.
3. Correct. AWS allows businesses to go global in minutes by deploying applications across multiple regions with a few clicks.
4. Incorrect. Constructing custom regional data centers requires heavy upfront capital and long timelines, which cloud avoids.
questions.topic: Cloud Concepts - Go Global in Minutes

questions.question: An enterprise is setting up a big data log processing and analytics pipeline on Amazon EC2 that requires low-cost HDD storage for large sequential streaming operations and high throughput, where performance is measured primarily by throughput rather than IOPS. Which Amazon EBS volume type is designed for this use case?
options: io2
gp3
st1
sc1
questions.explanation:
Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) volumes are optimized for large streaming workloads such as big data, data warehouses, and log processing, where the dominant performance attribute is throughput.

1. Incorrect: io2 is a Provisioned IOPS SSD designed for transactional, low-latency workloads rather than sequential streaming throughput.
2. gp3 can serve many workloads, but it is SSD storage rather than the requested throughput-oriented HDD option.
3. Correct: st1 is optimized for large streaming workloads, big data, and log processing requiring high sequential throughput.
4. Incorrect: sc1 is designed for infrequently accessed cold data and lowest storage cost, rather than active big data processing pipelines.
questions.topic: Determine high-performing and/or scalable storage solutions

questions.question: A DynamoDB Query returns LastEvaluatedKey even though the client has fewer records than it needs. How should the client continue the same query?
options: Replace the partition key with LastEvaluatedKey as a string
Pass LastEvaluatedKey as ExclusiveStartKey on the next request
Repeat the identical request without a start key and append its results
Treat LastEvaluatedKey as proof that no more data exists
questions.explanation:
DynamoDB paginates Query results. Continuing from the returned key retrieves later pages while retaining the same key conditions and other relevant query settings.

1. The continuation key is a structured pagination position, not a replacement partition-key value.
2. DynamoDB paginates Query results. Continuing from the returned key retrieves later pages while retaining the same key conditions and other relevant query settings.
3. That can repeatedly retrieve the first page.
4. A nonempty continuation key indicates that another request may be needed.

questions.question: An EC2-based Elastic Beanstalk environment should test a new application version on a fresh set of instances while retaining the existing fleet if the rollout fails. Which deployment policy best fits?
options: A configuration-only update with no application version
Immutable deployment
All at once
Rolling without an additional batch
questions.explanation:
Immutable deployments create replacement instances in a separate temporary group before accepting the release. Failure can leave the original fleet serving, at the cost of extra capacity during deployment.

1. That does not deploy the new application code.
2. Immutable deployments create replacement instances in a separate temporary group before accepting the release. Failure can leave the original fleet serving, at the cost of extra capacity during deployment.
3. All-at-once updates the existing fleet together and does not provide the stated replacement-fleet isolation.
4. That updates batches in the existing fleet and temporarily reduces available serving capacity.

questions.question: A team is evaluating an EMR Spark capacity increase. Which two measurements most directly establish whether the change improves the pipeline objective? Choose TWO.
options: End-to-end runtime against the delivery deadline
Total workload cost and resource utilization for the representative dataset
Only the number of provisioned instances, without measuring completed workload performance
Only driver CPU utilization, excluding executor activity and job duration
Only executor startup time, excluding all data processing stages
questions.explanation:
End-to-end runtime tests whether the user-facing delivery objective improves. Cost and utilization expose whether the improvement is efficient.

1. End-to-end runtime tests whether the user-facing delivery objective improves. Cost and utilization expose whether the improvement is efficient.
2. Representative cost and utilization reveal overprovisioning or remaining bottlenecks alongside runtime.
3. Instance count is a capacity input rather than evidence of meeting the pipeline deadline.
4. A single component metric cannot establish end-to-end delivery improvement or total efficiency.
5. Startup is just one phase and does not establish overall runtime or workload cost.

questions.question: A BI workload repeatedly joins large fact and dimension tables, scans many rows, and aggregates history. The team needs a managed SQL warehouse rather than per-item transactional access. Which store best matches?
options: ElastiCache as the sole durable warehouse for all history
An RDS read replica selected solely because it supports SQL, without evaluating analytical scale
Amazon Redshift with a suitable physical design and workload configuration
DynamoDB with full-table scans for every multi-table SQL join
questions.explanation:
Redshift is designed for analytical warehouse workloads and large-scale aggregations. Distribution, sort design, and workload management still determine performance.

1. A cache alone is not the durable analytical warehouse described.
2. SQL support alone does not establish suitability for large warehouse scans and joins.
3. Redshift is designed for analytical warehouse workloads and large-scale aggregations. Distribution, sort design, and workload management still determine performance.
4. DynamoDB is oriented toward keyed access patterns rather than these warehouse joins.

questions.question: You have a Google Cloud Storage (GCS) container named storage1 that contains the files shown in the following table. You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that has the cache for shortcuts enabled. Workspace1 contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1. Lakehouse1 has the shortcuts shown in the following table. You need to read data from all the shortcuts. Which shortcuts will retrieve data from the cache?
questions.scenario:
You have a Google Cloud Storage (GCS) container named storage1 that contains the files shown in the following table.

You have a Fabric workspace named Workspace1 that has the cache for shortcuts enabled. Workspace1 contains a lakehouse named Lakehouse1. Lakehouse1 has the shortcuts shown in the following table.

You need to read data from all the shortcuts.
options: Stores only
Products only
Stores and Products only
Products, Stores, and Trips
Trips only
Products and Trips only
questions.explanation: Shortcuts retrieve data from cache when they have been accessed within the cache retention period. Products (12 hours ago) and Stores (4 hours ago) are within the typical cache period, while Trips (48 hours ago) would likely need to retrieve from the original source.
